audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 and Levels 4-5 were marked 'Skill' where the packet chart gives both to Renekton, and the first-item and 2+ rows were given to Renekton where the packet says Skill and Tahm Kench. The page's own text already said the opposite: whys[5] calls the first-item stage 'genuinely coin-flip' and whys[6] says he outheals your damage.
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no dash at 1 and Tongue Lash only slows until three stacks; Renekton owns those levels. After items, Warmog and Heartsteel regen invert the lane.
audit.corrected: Levels 1 and 4-5 flipped to Renekton (7/10), first item to Skill (5/10), 2+ items to Tahm Kench (3/10), both layers, as one atomic group.

audit.why: Levels 2-3, level 6 Dominus, first item, and his 2-item HP scaling — four spikes, correctly placed. The mirror's finding that level 6 adds Devour as a removal is consistent with the level-6 row staying 'Skill'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (1) Devour is called his W ('his devour W', 'he can devour himself away'); Devour is R and Abyssal Dive is the W, a dive that knocks up. (2) Tongue Lash is called a root — it damages and slows, and only stuns once the target already carries three An Acquired Taste stacks. (3) Missing: empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields, so 50 Fury deletes the Thick Skin shield he converts stored damage into.
audit.why: The knockup on Abyssal Dive is what actually breaks your dash; the stun has a stack precondition you can play around; and the shield-destroy is the reason to arrive at 50 Fury rather than trade early.
audit.corrected: Slots fixed in whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid; the stun's stack condition stated in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and wants.foe[1]; shield destruction stated in phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and spikes[1].text — matching the mirror's wording.

edits.before: Fury autos bully the first waves. Identify how Tahm Kench contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Fury autos bully the first waves — he has no dash, and Tongue Lash only slows until three stacks land.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Abyssal Dive's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: trade only at 50 fury, because empowered W destroys the Thick Skin shield a smaller trade cannot break.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Tahm Kench carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in and his regen outpaces your flat burst — Tahm Kench carry threat 7/10, so take objectives, not the side-lane duel.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His escape + shield. Burst when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: 21s at rank 1, and it knocks up — that is what breaks your dash. - Tongue Lash: 7s, slows, and stuns only at three Acquired Taste stacks. - Thick Skin: empowered W destroys that shield outright.

edits.before: His escape + shield. Burst when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: A knockup dive, 21s at rank 1 — bait it out, then commit your dash.

edits.before: Track Tahm Kench's Abyssal Dive: His escape + shield. Burst when down. When it is down — W-stun + Q him.
edits.after: Empowered W destroys Thick Skin. Tongue Lash stuns only at three stacks — before that it is a slow.

edits.before: Dominus HP surge gives you a buffer but his devour W can interrupt your E approach; feint the engage to bait the W cooldown before you all-in.
edits.after: Dominus buffers you, but Abyssal Dive (W) knocks you up mid-approach — feint the engage to bait it, then all-in on its 21-second downtime.

edits.before: Dominus's HP surge makes his Q tongue-lash bounce off raw stats; run your full pattern but respect his devour W — it can eat your E approach mid-dash.
edits.after: Dominus's HP surge blunts Tongue Lash, and 50 Fury destroys the Thick Skin shield outright — run the pattern, but respect Abyssal Dive's knockup mid-dash.

edits.before: Land Q tongue-lash to lock you in place and follow with an auto-reset into a retrade he wins on raw HP
edits.after: Stack An Acquired Taste to three so Tongue Lash stuns instead of slowing, then retrade on raw HP

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you are still ahead but the lane is becoming attrition: every trade he walks away from he is converting a portion of the grey-health back via passive, so short trades hurt you more than full all-ins do. Commit to a full E-W-Q burst when Fury is stocked, then disengage with the return dash before he can retrade or land his Q tongue on you — that tongue root is the only thing that lets him win a prolonged exchange. At level 6, Dominus is your stat-check equaliser: the HP boost dwarfs his grey-health regen momentarily, but do not blow the ultimate into a half-health Tahm Kench expecting a kill — he can devour himself away from your combo or simply outlast you on the back end of R. Use R to survive a bad trade or to zone him off the wave, not as a pure kill cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you are still ahead but the lane is attrition: Thick Skin banks a share of everything you deal and heals it back out of combat, so short trades hurt you more than full all-ins. Commit the E-W-Q burst at 50 Fury — that is the version that destroys the Thick Skin shield — then leave on the return dash before he stacks An Acquired Taste to three and the slow becomes a stun. At level 6 Dominus is your stat check, but do not spend it expecting a kill: Abyssal Dive is a 21-second escape and knockup, and Devour can pull an ally out of your combo entirely. Use R to survive a bad trade or zone him off the wave.

notes: Ability slots were wrong on this page: Devour was called his W (it is R) and Abyssal Dive's knockup — the thing that actually interrupts your dash — was never mentioned. Tongue Lash was called a root; it slows, and only stuns at three An Acquired Taste stacks. The empowered-W shield destruction now matches the mirror tahmkench__renekton, which states the same interaction from the other side. Chart rows were moved to the packet chart; the mirror was audited before this one, so if its rows were left on the old values mirror-fix will need to reconcile Level 1, Levels 4-5, First item and 2+ items.
